motion.name: terminus-dock

components.css: .ds-route { --line: var(--cobalt, #2a62e0); --line-text: var(--cobalt-text, #8fb0ff); list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; color: var(--text, #f5f6f2); } .ds-station { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 28px 1fr; column-gap: 16px; } .ds-track { position: relative; min-height: 28px; } .ds-station:not(:last-child) .ds-track::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 11px; top: 14px; bottom: 0; width: 6px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--line); } .ds-station[data-cleared] .ds-track::after { background: var(--line); } .ds-mark { position: absolute; z-index: 1; top: 0; left: 0; width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--enamel, #0f1d3a); border: 5px solid var(--line); box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-station[data-state='done'] .ds-mark { background: var(--porcelain, #f5f6f2); } .ds-station[data-state='busy'] .ds-mark { background: var(--amber, #f2a900); border-color: var(--amber, #f2a900); } .ds-plate2 { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; padding-bottom: 24px; } .ds-name { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.375rem; line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-does { color: var(--text-muted, #a9b3c7); font-size: 0.9375rem; line-height: 1.4; max-width: 34ch; } .ds-state { margin-top: 4px; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.9375rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-muted, #a9b3c7); } .ds-station[data-state='done'] .ds-state { color: var(--line-text); } .ds-station[data-state='busy'] .ds-state { color: var(--amber, #f2a900); }

narrative.overview:
A payment is a ride on a transit map. The payer's wallet is a line; its setup steps are stations; the PayRouter contract is the interchange where the MetaMask and Solflare lines meet; the merchant is the terminus. Everything is drawn as flat signage on a midnight enamel wall: condensed capitals, round station marks, coloured line segments, a porcelain destination plate. Nothing glows, floats, or blurs.

The surface is dense with real information (amounts, fees, signature counts, hashes) but ordered like a platform sign: the destination plate first, then the line choice, then the route, then one large button that clears the next station. The colour of a line means the wallet; amber means something is happening now; scarlet means something failed. Those meanings never move.
keyCharacteristics: Midnight enamel wall with a single porcelain plate as the only light surface.
One lane colour at a time, set by `data-lane`, painting the route, the selected badge, and the primary button.
Station marks carry all step state; the name plates beside them never change wording.
Condensed transit capitals for every heading, label and button; mono only for data.
Flat: depth comes from tone (enamel-deep, enamel, enamel-raised, porcelain), never from shadow.

rules.name: The Lane Owns the Colour Rule
rules.body: Exactly one lane colour is live on a screen, set by `[data-lane]` on the page (`--line`, `--line-ink`, `--line-text`). Cobalt and green appear together only where both lines are drawn: the schematic and the other-wallet stub at the interchange.

rules.name: The Signal Reservation Rule
rules.body: Amber means "in progress or needs attention", scarlet means "failed". Neither is decoration, and neither is used for a lane.

rules.name: The Ink on Green Rule
rules.body: Text on a green fill is midnight enamel; text on cobalt is porcelain. Never white on green.

rules.name: The Signage Caps Rule
rules.body: Every heading, label, state word and button is Barlow Condensed in uppercase with positive tracking. Body sentences are never uppercase.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Mono is for addresses, hashes, amounts and counts only. Readout amounts carry the unit "USDC".

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: Light comes from porcelain and line colour, never from shadow, gradient or blur.

dos: Do set lane colour through `[data-lane]` and the `--line`, `--line-ink`, `--line-text` variables, never by hard-coding cobalt or green in a component.
Do put midnight enamel text on green and amber fills, porcelain text on cobalt.
Do express step state only through the station mark grammar (hollow, porcelain, muted, amber, scarlet strike) plus the state word.
Do keep one full-width next-station button per view, sticky on phones under 860px.
Do keep every target at least 44px and keep the amber 2px focus ring (ink inside the porcelain plate).
Do keep the arrival sweep the only expressive animation, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do write UI copy in English, with exact amounts and the unit "USDC" or "wUSDC".
donts: Don't add drop shadows, glows, gradients or blur; depth is tonal.
Don't use amber or scarlet for anything but pending and failed (amber also marks focus and testnet).
Don't show both lane colours as competing accents outside the schematic and the interchange stub.
Don't set sentences, prose states or labels in mono.
Don't round corners beyond 4px or use pill buttons; circles belong to station marks.
Don't bend lines at angles other than 45 and 90 degrees.
